content:
Maya Chen: heads up — alerting showed a jump of GPU nodes in us-west1-b to NotReady and they got a NoSchedule taint after last night's node image rollout. device-plugin DaemonSet is crashlooping on affected nodes. Anyone already looking?

infra-bot: ALERT: 28 gpu-nodes NotReady in cluster-prod-usw1 (us-west1-b). Autoscaler: scale activity blocked (tainted/unschedulable nodes). Logs attached to ticket: https://our.incident/INC-3981

Sam Patel: I'm on it. grabbed one node (gpu-node-07) — saw these errors in the device-plugin container: 

```
modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.19.0-101-generic
level=error msg="failed to start device plugin: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = \"connection error: desc = \\\"transport: error while dialing: dial unix /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock: connect: no such file or directory\\\"\""
```

Sam Patel: TL;DR looks like kernel/package mismatch: node got a kernel version that does not have the nvidia kernel module prebuilt. Device plugin tries to create the socket but kubelet never exposes GPU resources so plugin exits and (via our startup hooks) the node gets a taint to prevent scheduling.

Jules Rivera: Confirmed on another node: `kubectl describe node gpu-node-12` shows `Conditions: Ready False` and `Taints: nvidia.driver/unavailable:NoSchedule`. There are a handful of critical system pods pinned to those nodes (monitoring/logging) so autoscaler won't drain them.

Liam O'Connor: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rebuild kernel module on affected nodes (DKMS) and restart kubelet/device-plugin, 2) roll back node image to previous working bundle, 3) create a fresh node pool with driver baked in and cordon old nodes then migrate workloads. Which is fastest without hitting customer SLA?

Sam Patel: Tried `apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-535` on gpu-node-07 but DKMS failed because headers for the new kernel aren't present. Rebooting to previous kernel is possible but risky cluster-wide.

Maya Chen: For now we should avoid cluster-wide reboots. Proposal: spawn a small replacement node pool (same machine type) with the validated image (driver+module built), add it to rotation, and migrate critical system pods off bad nodes so autoscaler can consider scale-down. Yes it's an extra cost but minimizes customer risk. Estimated incremental cost: ~$4.2k/day if we keep 32 GPUs extra (rough back-of-envelope).

ops-oncall: +1 to new node pool. I'll approve the spend for the week. Sam/Jules — can you coordinate creation of pool `gpu-fix-2165` and smoke test with 2 nodes before we scale to full capacity? Put a hold on draining any PV-backed pods until migration plan is ready.

Jules Rivera: started terraform change to add node pool with image `redwood-gpu-2026-03-18-driver535` and node taints to keep it dedicated for now. Will run canary with 2 nodes first. I'll post logs here once the device plugin registers successfully.

Sam Patel: note for follow-up: need a root cause writeup — why the node image rollout picked a kernel without built modules. Suspect our image build pipeline missed DKMS step for the 5.19 build. Ticketing: INC-3981 assigned to eng-infra and eng-runtime for triage.

Maya Chen: thanks. once canary confirms, schedule gradual move and a guarded drain of old nodes. Also add a preflight that checks `modprobe nvidia` during image bake to prevent regression. :eyes:

infra-bot: NOTE: incident severity downgraded to SEV-3 after mitigation plan accepted.

ops-oncall: assigning follow-up tasks: create pool (Sam), bake image check (Jules), cost estimate (Maya). I'll run postmortem template.

Sam Patel: will post canary outcome in ~15m.

(--- thread ends)
